data.title: DLP Resources Launches Maiden Drill Program at Peru’s Esperanza Copper Project
data.description:
The latest update is out from DLP Resources ( (TSE:DLP) ).

DLP Resources has begun its first-ever diamond drill program at the 100%-owned Esperanza copper-gold-molybdenum project in southern Peru, marking the initial drilling on a sizeable, previously untested land package. The campaign, launched after permitting and rapid mobilization supported by strong local infrastructure, is designed to evaluate both shallow copper oxide mineralisation and a large porphyry system at depth.

The approximately 3,000-metre program will test a 300 m by 700 m near-surface copper oxide zone with four shallow holes, followed by three 800-metre holes into the main porphyry target beneath a 5.0 km by 2.5 km magnetic anomaly. Initial assay results are expected from the shallow holes, with deeper results to follow, and successful outcomes could materially advance DLP’s exploration pipeline and strengthen its position in Peru’s copper-focused mining corridor.

The company’s 100%-owned Esperanza project in southern Peru spans 22,500 hectares and benefits from established regional mining infrastructure, including road access, power and a skilled labour pool across the Arequipa and Moquegua regions.

Esperanza hosts a large 5.0 km by 2.5 km magnetic anomaly and a defined near-surface copper oxide zone, outlined by extensive mapping, trenching, geochemistry, geophysics and 503 surface rock chip samples. data.title: Healthcare Triangle Amends Equity Funding Agreement Terms
data.description:
Healthcare Triangle ( (HCTI) ) has issued an announcement.

On September 22, 2026, Healthcare Triangle amended its June 12, 2026 equity purchase agreement with Hudson Global Ventures, adjusting key financing terms that govern how the company can raise capital through equity puts to the investor. The changes refine the definitions of purchase price and valuation period, significantly lower the maximum amount per put notice from $2,500,000 to $250,000, and raise the minimum share price threshold from $0.01 to $0.10, while adding a new change-of-control clause that cuts off the company’s ability to issue additional put notices if control of the company shifts, potentially tightening but stabilizing its access to equity funding.

These revisions suggest Healthcare Triangle is rebalancing its capital-raising framework to limit large discounted issuances and protect share value, which may reduce dilution risk for existing shareholders and signal a more conservative funding approach. At the same time, the reduced flexibility in put size and the change-of-control limitation could constrain rapid equity financing during strategic transactions, affecting how the company can tap this facility for future growth or restructuring needs.
